name: Buzzer Beater DE
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the
transcription, the rewrite that turns speech into report, the stated
40px, the twenty characters to a line, the freeform text box, the
block at the foot of the frame, the card and the drag are all the same
and are named here rather than restated. Where it parts company with
Hall of Femme is the face, the colours, and a highlight that picks
words out by colour alone rather than by a second weight.
The DE in the name is the account's, the way the DE in Hall of Femme
DE, Fitness Story DE and Fight Source DE is: it says which of the
brand's feeds this is and not what language the app is in. What lands
on the frames is whatever the video's own voice track was saying, put
through the transcription and the rewrite exactly as on every channel
here; nothing in this pack changes that, and everything the app itself
says is English like the rest of it (see CLAUDE.md).
The glyph check the DE feeds before this one made a habit of, and this
face passes it with the same footnote Fight Source DE's does. Garamond
Premier Pro Bold Italic Subhead carries 1268 codepoints - the umlauts,
the eszett and the low quotes German sets speech in among them - so a
caption is drawn from the file rather than from whatever the browser
substitutes for a missing glyph, which would be a different face at a
width nothing measured. The footnote is the capital eszett: U+1E9E is
not in the file, and is never asked for, because the preset's
`uppercase` goes through toUpperCase (see `cased` in js/text.js) and
JavaScript maps a lower-case eszett to SS rather than to its capital.
A face chosen for how it looks in English is not automatically a face
that can SET another language, and the check is two minutes against a
cmap.
_comment_order: Last under the heading, which is where a new show goes: the numbers
are a running order rather than a ranking, and the foreign feeds have
been landing at the end of it since Hall of Femme DE took 920.
927 and not 926, which is the second time this has happened and is
worth recording as such. Fight Source DE's note says 924 was taken by
Re-belle between that pack being written and being saved; 926 was
taken by Beauty-Tipps between this one being written and being saved.
A shared number is not an error - the server breaks the tie
alphabetically by name (see serve.py) - it is simply an order nobody
chose, and Buzzer Beater DE would have sorted above Beauty-Tipps for
no reason. Two collisions in two new packs says the real answer is to
read the heading's last number at the moment of saving rather than at
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: What separates this show from the others under the heading: it is set
in Garamond Premier Pro Bold Italic Subhead, in a pale pink, a black
or a white the user pairs per frame, on a card, with picked words set
apart by a colour the user chooses rather than by a second face.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
freeform box, where the block stands on the frame, the drag, the shape
of the card, the word highlight - is the Snapchat caption design and
is stated once, in content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack
states what makes it this show.
It used to set the caption on the photograph, in the pink alone, with
a dark drop shadow, and wrote down that a bright still was the frame
it lost - and that the honest remedies were a card or a second
colour. The show has asked for both: colours for the letters AND for
a ground behind them, which is a request for a card, since the panel
palette cannot exist without one (see editor.paletteOf). So it is on
the card its carded siblings use, and what follows from that is
written once, in content/README.md, under 'A channel that set its
caption on the photograph may take the card back'.
It is also the one pack under this heading where the width matters,
and it was measured before the face was settled on - on the canvas
the renderer uses, so the numbers include the kerning. Twenty mixed
capitals in this face come out 499px against the 486px a line has,
where Korolev Bold's come out 434 - so here the frame's width and the
preset's twenty characters land in the same place rather than the
characters binding first. Ordinary prose still fits, because the
spaces and the narrow letters an alphabet run has none of do most of
the work: nineteen characters of real sentence measure 433px. What it
means in practice is that an unusually wide line breaks at nineteen
instead of twenty, which the wrapper does on its own and nobody sees
(see the two ceilings in js/caption.js). The measurements themselves
are in content/faces/garamond-premier-pro-bold-italic-subhead.json.
Uppercased, for the reason every one of its neighbours is: at 40px
with twenty characters to a line the caption is three short beats
rather than a paragraph, and capitals are what those are set in. It
costs this face more than it costs the others, and that is worth being
honest about - an italic of this kind is drawn around its lower case,
and its capitals are the calmer half of it. They are still italic
capitals, which almost nothing else on Snapchat is, and the preset's
`uppercase` is the guideline a pack may break with a reason (Killer
Bites does). This show has no such reason yet; the day it decides its
lower case IS the brand, `uppercase: false` is one line in this file.

_comment_color: The pale pink, and the channel's own answer: what every frame is
set in until somebody presses a swatch, since a frame stores no
colour of its own until it is given one (see state.textColorFor).
It opens the list in `colors` below, so the pink swatch is the one
shown as chosen on an untouched frame.
A pale pink is near the top of the lightness range, so on the
photograph a blown-out sky or a white jersey was where it went. On
a card it is read against a ground somebody chose instead, which

_comment_highlight: The preset's word highlight, set in the block's own face and its
own pink. Picked words are told apart by COLOUR, and the colour is
the user's, from the highlight row every palette now carries.
This show used to have none, and the reason was that a highlight
would have had to split a colour inside one sentence - which was
an argument against the pack choosing that colour, not against the
user doing so. The highlight row answers it: until it is pressed
on a frame, a picked word looks exactly like its neighbours and
follows the letters' colour, so nothing changes for anybody who
never reaches for it. Written down once, for all nine packs that
made this change, in content/README.md under 'Every palette
A second face is still not here. The roman of this family would
pick words out of the italic the way laugh-society-2 picks its
lines out, a change of voice rather than of colour; it is a second
file in fonts/ as well as a second face on one block, and the day
the show wants it, `highlight.face` is where it goes.
_comment_panel: Black, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
Black because it is the first colour the show asked for and a pale
pink is at its strongest on it - the dark edge the old drop shadow
gave each letter, given to the whole line instead. The white card
is a button away, under black type.
